children: The China-based AI startup Manus is currently engaged in a $500M funding round that would double its valuation to $4B, according to Bloomberg.

had agreed to acquire Manus for $2B late last year, but Chinese regulators blocked the deal, citing national security concerns. Now, Manus is engaged in a new funding round and is considering an initial public offering on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Manus develops AI agents capable of planning and executing long-range, multi-step tasks, such as building presentations or writing in-depth reports within a cloud sandbox environment.
Potential participants in the latest funding round include IDG Capital and Boyu Capital, the report said. Current backers such as Tencent
, HSG and ZhenFund are also considering participation. Manus is also eyeing a route to restructure the company for a possible IPO.
